title: Graphing Linear Relations: Tables of Values and Straight-Line Graphs
seo_title: Year 8 Linear Graphs Worksheets: Tables of Values, Gradient and Real-Life Linear Relations (Free, Answer Key)

meta_desc: Free Year 8 maths worksheets on graphing linear relations for the Australian Curriculum (AC9M8A02): tables of values, points on a line, equations from graphs, gradient and y-intercept, and real-life linear graphs. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: A linear relation makes a straight line. Use a table of values to plot it.
key_sub: In y = mx + c, c is where the line crosses the y-axis and m is how steep it is.
body_html:
How it works

A linear relation such as y = 2x + 1 gives a straight-line graph. Make a table of values: choose some x values, substitute to find each y, plot the points and join them with a ruler.

A point is on the line if its coordinates make the rule true. In y = mx + c, c is where the line crosses the y-axis and m (the gradient) tells you how steep it is: up m for every 1 across. A negative gradient slopes down from left to right.

Where two lines cross, both rules are true. Reading the crossing point is a graphical way to solve an equation.

Example

Complete the table for y = 3x − 2 when x = −1, 0, 1, 2.

Substitute each x: 3 × (−1) − 2 = −5, and so on.

Answer: −5, −2, 1, 4

Example

Is (4, 9) on the line y = 2x + 1?

2 × 4 + 1 = 9.

Answer: Yes

Example

Where do y = 2x + 1 and y = 7 meet?

2x + 1 = 7, so x = 3.

Answer: (3, 7)

Common mistakes

  • Swapping x and y when plotting or checking a point.
  • Losing a negative sign: when x = −2, 3x = −6.
  • Mixing up the gradient and the y-intercept in y = mx + c.
  • Thinking x = 3 is a horizontal line. It is vertical.

faq.q: How do I graph a linear relation?
faq.a: Make a table of values: choose a few x values, work out y for each, plot the points and join them with a straight line.

faq.q: How do I check if a point is on a line?
faq.a: Substitute the x-coordinate into the rule. If you get the y-coordinate, the point is on the line.

faq.q: What do m and c mean in y = mx + c?
faq.a: m is the gradient (how far the line goes up for each 1 across) and c is the y-intercept (where it crosses the y-axis).

faq.q: How can a graph solve an equation?
faq.a: Graph both sides as lines. The x-coordinate where they cross is the solution.

items.q: Which point lies on the line y = 4x + 5?
items.e: Substitute the x-coordinate: 4 × 0 + 5 = 5, which matches. So (0, 5).

items.q: Which point lies on the line y = 3x + 3?
items.e: Substitute the x-coordinate: 3 × (−2) + 3 = −3, which matches. So (−2, −3).

items.q: Which point lies on the line y = −3x + 1?

items.e: It crosses the y-axis at 0, so c = 0. For every 1 across it goes up 3, so m = 3. y = 3x.

items.q: A taxi fare in Brisbane is given by C = 2d + 3, where d is kilometres. What does the 3 represent?
items.e: When d = 0, C = 3. It is the fixed charge you pay before travelling.

items.q: A taxi fare is given by C = 2d + 3, where d is kilometres. What does the 2 represent?
items.e: The gradient is the rate of change: each extra kilometre costs $2.

items.q: A candle is 20 cm tall and burns 2 cm every hour. Which equation gives its height h after t hours?
items.e: Start at 20 and go down 2 each hour: h = 20 − 2t, a negative gradient.

items.q: A plumber charges a $40 call-out fee plus $25 per hour. Which equation gives the cost C for h hours?
items.e: $25 for each hour, plus $40 once: C = 25h + 40.

items.q: The line y = 3x − 6 crosses the x-axis at…
Which line is steepest?
items.e: Steepness depends on the size of the gradient, ignoring its sign. |−5| is the biggest: y = −5x + 1.

items.q: Which line slopes down from left to right?
items.e: A negative gradient slopes down: y = 7 − 2x has gradient −2.

items.q: Does the point (3, 11) lie on y = 4x − 1?
items.e: Substitute x = 3: 12 − 1 = 11, which matches. Yes.

items.q: A phone plan costs $15 a month plus 10c per minute. What is the gradient of the graph of cost ($) against minutes?
items.e: Each minute adds 10c = $0.10, so the gradient is 0.1.

items.q: 1 Australian dollar is worth 0.6 euros. On a graph of euros against Australian dollars, what is the gradient?
items.e: Euros = 0.6 × dollars, a straight line through (0, 0) with gradient 0.6.

items.q: A line has gradient 2 and passes through (0, −4). What is its equation?
Which two lines are parallel?
items.e: Parallel lines have the same gradient: 3x in both.

items.q: Where do y = 2x + 1 and y = 7 meet?
items.e: 2x + 1 = 7, so x = 3. They meet at (3, 7).

items.q: A water tank holds 500 litres and drains at 25 litres per minute. After how many minutes is it empty?
What is the gradient of a horizontal line?
items.e: A horizontal line does not go up or down, so its gradient is 0.

items.q: The line through (1, 4) and (3, 10) has equation…
What is the gradient of the line?
items.e: From (0, −1) to (1, 1) the line goes up 2 for 1 across: gradient 2.

items.q: What is the gradient of the line?
items.e: It goes down 1 for every 2 across: gradient −12.

items.q: What is the equation of the line?
items.e: It crosses the y-axis at 1 and goes down 1 for each 1 across: y = −x + 1.

items.q: What is the equation of the line?
items.e: Every point has y = −2, so y = −2.
